checks.description: The catalog schema file parses as JSON and declares every generated record field, so the generate step can validate records against it.
checks.expected: The schema file parses, schema.properties covers id plus all generated fields, and the check prints the field count.
checks.procedure: node -e "const fs=require('fs');const s=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('registry/schema/catalog-v3.schema.json','utf8'));const need=['id','name','kind','description','source','origin','install_cmd','version_pin','category','tags','when_to_use','phase','tier','verify_cmd','cost_note','verification','default_selected'];const missing=need.filter(function(f){return !s.properties||!s.properties[f]});if(missing.length>0)throw new Error('schema omits '+missing.join(','));console.log('schema-parse: '+need.length+' fields declared')"

description: ONE tiny verifier-gate smoke benchmark for the catalog schema file. It exists so a gate has something deterministic to run, not so anyone has a number to chase.
goodhart_guard: Keep this benchmark small on purpose. A benchmark that grows into a target stops measuring and starts distorting: entries get tuned to the metric instead of the work. This file stays at exactly one check; propose a second file rather than extending this one.
output_note: Outputs are illustrative and environment-dependent (~): field counts and timings vary by machine and schema version. They are never a target metric and never a release gate on their own.
